ours.text: k6: '...a late-week liquidity grab and reversal by Friday could produce a bullish turnaround supported by massive sideline capital in the US'
ours.problem: Conflates two separate arguments. The Friday reversal is a short-term scenario; sideline capital is a medium/long-term argument ('only a question of when').
Omission rather than contradiction: the creator 'bought one position yesterday just purely on the technicals', which is a new entry, not just a hold.

leapedge.text: 'a 4-5% move would likely test the $20-21 range (implied as 59-60 in transcript), while a 10-15% move could push prices toward $18-19 (implied as 53-54)'
leapedge.problem: Fabricated numbers. The creator says 59.60 and 54-53/55; $20-21 and $18-19 appear nowhere, and 'implied as' openly admits the substitution. A PM acting on this has wrong levels by ~3x.
The creator says '5% on the 10-year, that's the magical line', a threshold, not a print. Overstated.

Misstates direction. The creator bought a position yesterday and will not sell silver or miners; he is cautious about adding, not avoiding. A 'target' of 54-60 on an avoid idea is a downside scenario mislabelled as a target.

leapedge.text: 'clearer market signals emerge after the Fed decision later in the week'
leapedge.problem: Roughly right, though the creator specifically flags the second half of Friday's trading session.

sentimentIssues: 18 tickerSentiment rows with no ticker for any row; silver appears 6 times with stances flipping between bearish/watch, bearish/hold, bullish/watch and bearish/neutral.

Gold appears 5 times (bearish x3, bullish x2) with no horizon field to explain that bearish is short-term and bullish is medium-term. Add a horizon so the split reads as coherent rather than contradictory.
The 'precious metals' and 'oil' rows are commentary, not stances. They are fine as context but add noise.
The silver 'hold' row is sound; it just needs the 'bought one position yesterday' nuance.
why: Ours faithfully records every level (gold 4,215; silver ~60 fakeout and 54-55 breakdown; 10y 5%; 30y breakout), the hold on silver and miners, and the energy holdings. LeapEdge fabricates silver prices ($20-21, $18-19) in a key point and mislabels a long-but-cautious creator as 'avoid'. Ours still misses the fresh technical buy and floods tickerSentiment with 18 unresolved, flip-flopping rows.
recommendations: Resolve macro assets to canonical symbols (silver->XAGUSD, gold->XAUUSD, dollar->DXY, 10y->US10Y) so the rows can join to price data. Currently every row is ticker null.
Add a horizon to each tickerSentiment row (short-term bearish, medium/long-term bullish) and merge per asset. Gold 'bearish' at 123s and 'bullish' at 317s is one view with two horizons, not two rows.
Capture fresh position changes explicitly: add action = bought/added/trimmed/holding with a date. 'I bought one position yesterday just purely on the technicals' should appear in the silver call.

Structure scenario levels as fields: support 'lower channel + 50DMA', fakeout_level ~59.60 (−4-5%), breakdown_level 54-55 (−10-15%), gold_downside 4,215, and a trigger ('Friday afternoon reversal candle -> be in').
Drop duplicated diagnostic omissions (source-0..4 are printed twice in this brief) and generic filler like 'No external pricing feeds...' from the user-facing brief.

Keep this strength against LeapEdge: never convert or 'normalise' creator levels. LeapEdge's '$20-21 (implied as 59-60)' is exactly the failure to avoid; add a test that asserts every number in keyPoints appears in the transcript.
